root_cause.text: The futex private default hash allocation logic in `need_futex_hash_allocate_default()` incorrectly assumed `mm` sharing only happened with `CLONE_THREAD|CLONE_VM`, so `mm->futex_ref` percpu allocation was skipped for other `CLONE_VM` sharers, violating its non-concurrency assumptions and allowing stale/freed percpu counters to be used.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states the function was “abusing `CLONE_THREAD`,” that this “breaks the non-concurrency assumptions when doing the `mm->futex_ref` pcpu allocations,” causing a KASAN “slab-use-after-free in `futex_hash_put`” where “the +1 bias can end up on a percpu counter that `mm->futex_ref` no longer points at”; the patch changes the check from requiring `(CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM)` to allowing any `CLONE_VM` clone except `CLONE_VFORK`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allocate the default futex hash for all `CLONE_VM` siblings except `vfork`, fixing overly restrictive handling that previously required `CLONE_THREAD`.
intent_record.what: The helper function `need_futex_hash_allocate_default(u64 clone_flags)` was simplified from an explicit `if`/`return` check requiring both `CLONE_THREAD` and `CLONE_VM` to a single boolean return expression that instead checks for `CLONE_VM` being set and `CLONE_VFORK` being unset, and a comment was added explaining that a default futex hash should be allocated for any sibling sharing the parent's `mm` except `vfork`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, default futex hash allocation now applies to more clone cases: it is no longer limited to thread clones with both `CLONE_THREAD` and `CLONE_VM`, but to any clone sharing the parent's memory space via `CLONE_VM` unless it is a `vfork`. This changes the allocation decision for non-thread `CLONE_VM` siblings and prevents allocation for `CLONE_VFORK` cases.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove a redundant comment about default futex hash allocation in copy_process() without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: A three-line explanatory comment immediately preceding the need_futex_hash_allocate_default(clone_flags) check and futex_hash_allocate_default() call in copy_process() was removed, while the surrounding code logic remained unchanged.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior, control flow, or functionality; it only removes inline documentation describing when the default futex hash is allocated.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by broadening default futex hash allocation from only CLONE_THREAD|CLONE_VM cases to all CLONE_VM sharers except vfork, matching the issue where non-thread CLONE_VM sharing skipped mm->futex_ref allocation and led to unsafe percpu counter use.
The change only removes a redundant comment and does not alter the futex hash allocation logic, mm sharing assumptions, or percpu futex_ref allocation behavior that caused the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This condition is the direct root cause: it only enables default futex hash allocation when both CLONE_THREAD and CLONE_VM are set, wrongly excluding other CLONE_VM sharers. That omission skips mm->futex_ref percpu allocation for valid mm-sharing cases, leading to unsafe use under concurrency assumptions.

When the overly restrictive clone_flags check matches non-threaded CLONE_VM sharers, this return causes the default futex hash allocation to be skipped, which is the immediate behavior enabling stale/freed percpu futex_ref usage.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition is the root cause: it only permits the default futex hash allocation path when both CLONE_THREAD and CLONE_VM are present, incorrectly excluding other CLONE_VM mm-sharing cases. As a result, mm->futex_ref percpu allocation is skipped for valid sharers, breaking the non-concurrency assumptions and enabling stale/freed percpu counter use.

This return is the harmful effect of the overly restrictive clone_flags check. For non-threaded CLONE_VM sharers, it causes need_futex_hash_allocate_default() to decline default futex hash allocation, leaving mm->futex_ref unallocated or improperly managed and allowing unsafe stale/freed percpu usage.

Author: Sebastian Andrzej Siewior <bigeasy@linutronix.de>

    futex: Allow automatic allocation of process wide futex hash
    
    Allocate a private futex hash with 16 slots if a task forks its first
    thread.
    
    Signed-off-by: Sebastian Andrzej Siewior <bigeasy@linutronix.de>
    Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>

bic_trace_step.reason: The added helper `need_futex_hash_allocate_default(u64 clone_flags)` makes the decision solely from clone flags: `if ((clone_flags & (CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM)) != (CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM)) return false; return true;`. This means allocation happens only when both `CLONE_THREAD` and `CLONE_VM` are set. The stated root cause is that this logic incorrectly assumed all `mm` sharing relevant to futex hashing occurs only with `CLONE_THREAD|CLONE_VM`, and therefore skipped `mm->futex_ref` percpu allocation for other `CLONE_VM` sharers. The vulnerable construct is therefore present in this function exactly as described. The call site in `copy_process()` uses that helper directly: `if (need_futex_hash_allocate_default(clone_flags)) { retval = futex_hash_allocate_default(); ... }`, so non-thread `CLONE_VM` sharers will not trigger allocation. No broader condition accounting for other `CLONE_VM` sharing cases is present, so the fix is not yet included.
